question: What is the primary goal of health education in nursing practice?

options.A: Ensuring strict hospital compliance with drug administration
options.B: Reducing the overall financial cost of running a clinic
options.C: Replacing the role of physicians in community diagnoses
options.D: Enabling patients to voluntarily adopt healthy behaviours

explanation: Health education aims to empower individuals and communities to make informed choices that promote and maintain their own wellness. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is health education considered essential for long-term patient recovery?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for surgical interventions
options.B: It addresses the root environment and habits causing illness
options.C: It eliminates the need for any follow-up clinical visits
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience a relapse

explanation: Clinical treatments only fix acute problems; education ensures patients change the lifestyle habits that led to the health crisis initially. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which principle states that teaching should focus on the learner's immediate needs?
explanation: Relevance ensures that the information shared directly matters to the daily life and concerns of the learner. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: A nurse teaching mothers about malaria prevention allows them to demonstrate how to tuck in mosquito nets. Which principle is applied here?
explanation: Having the learners physically practice the skill involves them actively rather than just listening passively. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: What must a nurse assess first before starting a formal teaching session with a patient in pain?

options.A: Available space in the ward corridor
options.B: The exact financial income of the household
options.D: The patient's highest level of formal education

explanation: Severe pain and physical distress impair concentration and prevent effective learning and retention of new health information. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h3)

question: An anxious patient refuses to listen to discharge instructions about wound care. What type of readiness is lacking?
explanation: High anxiety creates a psychological barrier that prevents the patient from engaging with emotional or mental preparation for learning. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which teaching method is most appropriate for teaching a patient how to self-administer insulin injections?

options.A: Listening to an audio recording alone
options.B: A large community lecture on diabetes

explanation: Psychomotor skills require the nurse to show the correct technique and the patient to practice it back to ensure safety. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the main advantage of group teaching sessions during antenatal clinic visits?

options.A: They foster peer support and shared learning experiences
options.B: They allow the nurse to ignore individual patient questions
options.C: They ensure every patient receives identical medical diagnoses
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for visual aids

explanation: Groups allow expectant mothers to learn from one another's questions and experiences while building a supportive community. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h4)

question: How should a nurse adjust teaching for an elderly patient with significant visual impairment?

options.B: Use large-print materials and clear verbal explanations
options.C: Speak extremely loudly without any visual aids
options.D: Provide dense textbook chapters for independent reading

explanation: Compensating for poor vision involves enlarging print sizes and relying more heavily on spoken communication. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the best approach when a patient is overwhelmed by fear and unable to process complex diagnosis details?

options.A: Stop all communication and leave the patient alone forever
options.B: Force the patient to listen until they understand everything
options.C: Ask family members to scold the patient into compliance
options.D: Break information into small chunks over multiple short sessions

explanation: Overwhelmed patients process information slowly, so delivering small, manageable pieces of education over time prevents cognitive overload. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is asking 'Do you understand?' an ineffective way to evaluate learning?

options.A: It usually elicits a polite nod without proving comprehension
options.B: It proves that the nurse failed to use visual aids
options.C: It violates professional nursing ethics regulations
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy clinic shift

explanation: Patients often say yes out of politeness or intimidation, even when they are completely confused by the instructions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: A nurse wants to prove a diabetic patient mastered dietary guidelines. What is the most reliable evaluation method?

options.A: Asking the patient to plan a sample daily meal menu
options.B: Checking if the patient nodded during the lecture
options.C: Asking a family member if they liked the talk
options.D: Reading the patient's hospital admission chart again

explanation: Having the patient apply the knowledge by planning a meal demonstrates actual comprehension far better than passive agreement. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which role does the nurse assume when helping a patient navigate emotional blocks through active listening?
explanation: Counseling involves supporting patients emotionally and helping them process feelings related to their health condition. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h7)

question: What does it mean for a nurse to act as an advocate during health education?

options.A: Making all healthcare decisions on behalf of the patient
options.B: Selling commercial wellness products inside the ward
options.C: Ensuring health information is accessible and respecting autonomy
options.D: Reporting patients who fail to follow medical advice

explanation: Advocacy in education means fighting for the patient's right to clear information and supporting their right to make informed choices. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h7)
